name: ParserPool::parse

test_list.description: Fingerprint a successfully parsed 20k-deep Rust tree in under three seconds; no repeated ancestor depth scans.
Shared iterative traversal matches native preorder nodes and visible depths for every supported grammar, including subtree skipping.
Rust, Python, C++, CUDA and TypeScript samples parse without error nodes and keep their source bytes.
Each grammar crate loads into a tree-sitter 0.27 parser (ABI 13..=15); a mismatch would surface as GrammarVersionMismatch.
A source of max_source_bytes parses; one byte more returns TooLarge { limit }.
A zero timeout returns ParseTimeout and the cancelled parser is reset, so the next parse is correct.
A leading UTF-8 BOM is ignored by the grammar but spans stay byte offsets of the original text.
Parsing with a previous tree yields the same tree as a full parse for edits, deletions, insertions and emptying the file.
A previous Parsed of a different language is not used for the incremental reparse.
50k-deep nesting in every language returns Ok or ParseFailed/ParseTimeout and every walk survives the deep tree.
Eight threads sharing one pool produce identical trees.
Property: arbitrary bytes in any language never panic; Ok keeps the source, Err is ParseFailed or ParseTimeout.
Property: incremental reparse equals a full parse for generated valid edits.

inputs.name: prev
inputs.description: Previous parse of the same file for incremental reparse.

output_description: Tree plus the original source bytes, or TooLarge / ParseTimeout / ParseFailed / GrammarVersionMismatch.
